Identifiable when: At least 2–3 independently processed replicates from the same local unit
Common confounding failure: Analytical uncertainty is absorbed into residual variance

Identifiable when: Multiple stations/reaches within each anchor or corridor stratum
Common confounding failure: Station effect is inseparable from anchor effect when one station exists per anchor

Identifiable when: Multiple anchors observed under comparable regime/time strata
Common confounding failure: Anchor effect is inseparable from season, event, or access effects when anchors are sampled once

Identifiable when: Multiple segments, with anchors nested within each
Common confounding failure: Corridor and local substrate/management effect are confounded if only one segment per corridor is measured

Identifiable when: Same anchors or stations revisited in multiple seasons/regimes
Common confounding failure: Season is confounded with a one-time equipment, protocol, or source change

Identifiable when: Multiple events per station/anchor and repeated reference windows
Common confounding failure: One monsoon event cannot estimate an event-level variance component

Identifiable when: Cross-over or co-location design with multiple devices at shared stations
Common confounding failure: Device bias is misclassified as spatial or temporal variation
